subject: Food Science
title: Starch Gelatinization
description: A fast breakdown of Starch Gelatinization for builders.

hook.text: Raw flour is gritty and inedible. Cook it with water and it becomes a smooth, thick sauce. That's gelatinization.

buildup.text: Starch granules are packed tight with amylose and amylopectin. In cold water, they just sit there.

discovery.text: Heat above 60°C makes starch granules absorb water and swell. The orderly structure breaks apart—thickening the liquid.

twist.text: Overcook the starch and the granules burst completely—your sauce gets thin again. That's called breakdown.

climax.text: Cornstarch thickens at lower temperatures than flour. That's why it's preferred for glossy Asian-style sauces.

punchline.text: Starch plus heat plus water equals thick. Overshoot and it thins out.

quiz.question: What happens during starch gelatinization?
options: Starch granules absorb water and swell, thickening the liquid
